html:
Murder of the emperor Caligula by officers of the Praetorian Guard in Rome on 24 January 41 CE.

Caligula was hated by the senate and had mocked his own guards. Cassius Chaerea, a tribune of the guard whom he teased for a weak voice, led the plot. They stabbed Caligula in a covered passage near the palace after a day of games. His wife Caesonia and young daughter were killed too.

The senate talked of restoring the republic. The guards had other ideas. They found Caligula's uncle Claudius hiding in the palace, carried him to their camp, and hailed him as emperor, in return for a payment. The senate gave way.

It was the first time the guard chose an emperor, and the rewards they won showed what the post was worth. See tiberius for the guard's earlier rise.
sum: Murder of the emperor Caligula by officers of the Praetorian Guard in Rome on 24 January 41 CE.
